newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end within reach of all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end within reach of all-time high.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index closed within reach of its all-time high on Wednesday, boosted by conglomerates and banks as the Canadian market sought to match Wall Street's recent gains.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished 47 points higher at 6307.13, near its record high of 6348.02 set on March 11.
"We're verging on breaking into new high ground in Toronto," said Ron Meisels, a Montreal-based portfolio consultant.
However Toronto failed to match New York's recent gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average hit a record of 7382 points on May 14 and surged one percent on Tuesday.
"We're in a bull market," Meisels said.
He added if Wall Street stayed in positive territory, "we could have a few up days without any effort."
Wednesday's trading was brisk at 98.7 million shares worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).
The conglomerate and utilities sectors led the charge, followed by oils, industrial products and banks. Four of Toronto's 14 sub-indices slipped: retail, golds, consumer products and base metals.
Advancing issues outnumbered declines 551 to 426, while 301 closed flat.
Among hot stocks telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc., Canada's largest publicly traded firm, rose 1 to close at 36.

Tee-Comm Electronics Inc. dropped 0.21 to 0.68, losing more ground after Wednesday's announcement that Bank of Montreal was reviewing the status of the satellite television provider's demand credit facility.
Tee-Comm dropped to penny stock status in recent weeks as news of financial difficulties leaked out.
Telecommunications firm Northern Telecom Ltd. rose 6.40 to 115, topping Toronto's net gainers.
